Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 21-Dec-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  Social Networks [CSE_4204]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                    Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Evaluate how adjacency matrices and edge lists represent the same network structure, and               (5)  
  compare their effectiveness for various types of network analysis tasks. Assess the advantages  
  A)           and limitations of each representation method, and justify which format provides better insights for  
  analyzing complex or large-scale networks using a suitable example.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Apply appropriate data preprocessing techniques to illustrate how missing or noisy data in real-       (3)  
  world network datasets can affect the accuracy of network analysis and community detection  
  results.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Apply Gephi or NetworkX to construct and visualize a social or communication network, and              (2)  
  identify key structural properties such as node degree, clustering, and network density to show  
  how relationships among individuals are represented.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Evaluate the strength of weak ties in facilitating information flow and opportunity discovery          (5)  
  within social structures. Assess how weak connections contribute to bridging otherwise  
  A)           disconnected communities and justify their role in enhancing network diversity.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Apply the concept of homophily to identify how similarities among individuals-such as shared           (3)  
  interests or demographics-influence the formation of social connections within a network.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Apply the concept of balance theory to identify how positive and negative relationships influence      (2)  
  the stability of small social groups.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)                Evaluate the effectiveness of different centrality measures-degree, closeness, betweenness, and (5)  
  eigenvector-in identifying influential nodes within a network. Justify which measure provides the  
  A)           most comprehensive insight for real-world applications like social influence or information diffusion.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  Page #1

B)         Apply the concept of hubs and authorities to identify how information importance is distributed in (3)  
  a web or citation network, and illustrate how the HITS algorithm helps distinguish between content  
  creators (hubs) and trusted sources (authorities).  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)         Apply the concept of cascading behavior to identify how an initial piece of information can trigger (2)  
  a chain reaction of adoption or sharing within a social network.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)              Compare and justify how the rich-get-richer mechanism leads to the formation of scale-free            (5)  
  structures in growing networks. Assess its implications for inequality and node influence within  
  A)         large-scale information or social systems.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)         Construct examples of different network topologies-such as random, small-world, and scale-free (3)  
  networks-to demonstrate how structural differences influence the speed and reach of epidemic  
  spreading.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)         Construct a simple example to illustrate how the power-law degree distribution characterizes          (2)  
  node connectivity in a scale-free network.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5)              Evaluate how the small-world property influences information diffusion, collaboration, and        (5)  
  innovation in large social or technological networks. Propose how understanding this property can  
  A)         be applied to optimize communication systems or design resilient network structures.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)         Apply your understanding of information diffusion models to construct a set of network-based          (3)  
  strategies-such as targeting pseudocores or key connectors-that can enhance the likelihood of  
  viral spread in digital marketing or awareness campaigns.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)         Apply your understanding of viral diffusion to interpret one real-world case-such as the spread of (2)  
  a popular hashtag or challenge-and explain how network structure contributed to its rapid growth.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  
  -----End-----
